This petition is filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C to enlarge the petitioner/A.3 on bail in connection with Cr.No.588/2020 on the file of II] Town Police Station,
Podugu Suresh vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 September, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84844015/

sentences.text: 2. The prime allegation made against this petitioner is that the petitioner is the supplier of cigarettes and pan masala to the kirana and pan shops and eking out his livelihood by doing supply business.
The petitioner/A.3 was found in possession of tobacco, gutka and khainee and arrested along with A.2 who was in possession of ganja of 4 kgs., besides seizing the cell phone and banned items.

The products which are being transported will not come under the definition of food as per Section 3(j)
of FSS Act.
cigarettes, chewing tobacco, pan masala and chewing material with tobacco, are included in the tobacco products.
The tobacco products are only defined under COTPA Act and not under FSS Act.
3. Therefore, possessing the items referred above is not an offence punishable under Section 3(j) of FSS Act.

Even to attract the offences punishable under Sections 270, 273, 328 read with 34 IPC,
Sections 20(b) read with 8(c) of NDPS Act, 1985 and Sections 59(i), 59(ii) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, there must be some material to show that those items consisting of poisonous substances endangered to the life of human being, but no such allegation is found in the entire material including the report.

Therefore, prima facie, I find no material against the petitioner to establish the offences punishable under Sections 27 O, 273, 328 read with 34 IPC, Section 20(b)
read with 8(c) of NDPS Act, 1985 and Sections 59(i), 59(ii) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the quantity of Ganja found in possession of petitioner is not commercial quantity,
consequently Section 37 of the NDPS Act, 1985 has no applicability apart from that, tobacco products sale or possession is not an offence of FSS Act as held by the Court.

Therefore, taking into consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, including languishing of petitioner in jail since 03.07.2020 for possessing the items referred above, the petitioner/A.3 can be enlarged on bail.

4. In the result, Criminal Petition is allowed granting bail to the petitioner/A.3 on executing a self-bond for Rs.50,000/- with two sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the learned IV Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Visakhapatnam.
